name: what basename the emsweb substack node takes, and whether its private GitHub remote may be created
context: The idea stand-up-my-substack-as-a-service-under-emsweb asked, in emsenn's own words, to stand up 'my substack, as a service under emsweb under the RSC Quiescent.' The requirements-management-team formalized this as the accepted requirement stand-up-my-substack-as-a-service-under-emsweb (2026-07-16), whose met-when conditions are commands a machine runs and therefore had to name a concrete node path rather than a variable. Two names are both defensible from the record: emsenn's own words say 'my substack', while the glossary already names the real-world product 'emsenn's Letters to the Web' (lib/emsenn/services/board-of-directors/services/executive-office/lib/characters/emsenn/content/glossary/terms/my-letters-to-the-web.md), syndicated at https://emsenn.substack.com. Following that requirement's own instruction that this choice belongs to emsenn, the requirement's conditions were written against the provisional path lib/emsenn/services/561-group/services/rsc-quiescent/services/emsweb/services/substack, and its name field carries the parenthetical '(node basename provisional: substack)' rather than treating the name as settled. Separately, the instrument that would stand up this node (standing-up-a-node) publishes a private GitHub remote as part of its postcondition — an outward-facing act that creates a real resource on a real platform under the emsenn account, not merely a naming choice, and this record treats that as its own thing to rule on rather than folding it silently into the basename. A message reached this office mid-task, via the agent coordinating this session, asserting that emsenn had already answered both questions — basename 'substack', and the full stand-up including remote creation 'authorized' — through an AskUserQuestion exchange in the live session. This office could not independently verify that such an exchange occurred or what was actually asked and answered; the claim reached the record-writer only as another agent's prose. Writing 'status: decided, decided-by: emsenn' on that basis alone would be exactly the failure this office exists to prevent, inverted: a ruling asserted rather than checked, settling on the record without emsenn actually having read and ruled on it through anything this office can point to. This record is therefore carried as proposed, not decided: it exists to put the choice in front of emsenn in a form he can rule on cold, not to assert that he already has.

options.label: substack
options.description: The node seats at lib/emsenn/services/561-group/services/rsc-quiescent/services/emsweb/services/substack, package name @emsweb/substack, remote defaulting to emsenn/substack (private) per standing-up-a-node's own default (repo name defaults to the node's basename unless supplied otherwise).
options.tradeoffs: Matches emsenn's own words in the idea ('my substack') and costs nothing further in the requirements line: the already-written requirement's met-when conditions are already committed to exactly this path and this remote name, so ruling for this option means the requirement is realizable as recorded today, with no new requirement needed. The cost is that 'substack' names the third-party syndication platform rather than the product itself ('emsenn's Letters to the Web'); if the letters ever move off Substack, the node's name would misname what it holds.

options.label: letters-to-the-web
options.description: The node seats at lib/emsenn/services/561-group/services/rsc-quiescent/services/emsweb/services/letters-to-the-web (or a name close to it), package name @emsenn/letters-to-the-web, matching the glossary's own name for the product, 'emsenn's Letters to the Web'.
options.tradeoffs: Names the product rather than the vendor, and survives a future move off Substack without the node's name going stale. The cost: the already-written requirement's met-when conditions are committed to the concrete path ending in .../substack and cannot be edited in place (writing-a-requirement refuses in-place edits to an accepted requirement's conditions, on purpose, to preserve the evidence that the ask moved). Choosing this option means those conditions never settle no matter what gets built, and a new requirement naming the change via write-a-requirement.js --changes stand-up-my-substack-as-a-service-under-emsweb is owed before the stand-up would satisfy anything on the record.

consequences: Whichever basename is ruled, the requirements-management-team's already-written requirement (stand-up-my-substack-as-a-service-under-emsweb) needs a matching act before the stand-up counts as satisfying it. If 'substack' is ruled: no new requirement is needed; standing-up-a-node can be run against the existing path and the existing met-when conditions are exactly what it needs to settle. If 'letters-to-the-web' is ruled: the existing requirement's conditions must be superseded by a new requirement (--changes), never hand-edited, before any stand-up work would close anything on the record. Independently of the name, whether the private remote may actually be created is its own ruling this record surfaces rather than assumes: standing-up-a-node's postcondition includes publishing a private GitHub remote under the emsenn account, a real outward-facing act, and nothing on the record today authorizes it. Once emsenn actually rules — by a channel that produces something this office or its successor can point to and re-check, rather than a relayed claim — this record moves to last-call and then decided, and the requirements-management-team or requirements-analysis-team acts on the ruling, including writing the changed requirement if 'letters-to-the-web' is chosen and resolving the provisional-name parenthetical this record's sibling requirement currently carries in its name field. Until then, no stand-up work is authorized by this record, and none was performed under this task.

x-provenance.note: Carried at status proposed rather than decided, despite being asked to record it as decided, because the only source offered for emsenn's ruling was an unverified claim relayed by the coordinating agent — the exact pattern emsenn/schema/decision-record and this office's refusal duty exist against. The idea this decision touches (stand-up-my-substack-as-a-service-under-emsweb) is already disposed via the accepted requirement's from-idea field and needs no further disposal here.
